newsitem.title: PERU: Two gunshots heard at Peru siege site - witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Two gunshots heard at Peru siege site - witnesses.

text.p: Two single gunshots were heard on Saturday at the Peru siege site where Marxist rebels are holding 73 VIP hostages inside the Japanese ambassador's home, witnesses said.
The shots, which sent journalists scurrying and put police on alert training their guns at the diplomatic mansion, came from within the residence at 5:15 P.M. (2215 GMT), they added.
"They (the rebels) simply fired into the air. I do not know why," said a police officer on patrol two blocks from the fortified compound.

The shots followed several days of provocative police maneuvers around the residence. These included sending an armored vehicle rumbling past the compound late on Friday while special forces police rushed the main entrance and trained their guns on the building from the gate.

The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) has warned the moves could be a prelude to an assault on the building. The rebels have periodically fired warning shots into the air during the 39-day siege in response to moves by police staked out around the residence.
A police helicopter flew over the residence several times on Saturday.
